Live token 2026-09-25 ~01:38Z: exp 1790329117 = 09:38:37Z (8 h).

Live login anh.tran@example.com at http://localhost:8080: token has two dots. `cut -d. -f1 | tr '_-' '/+' | base64 -d` -> {"alg":"HS256","typ":"JWT"} rc=0; -f2 -> {"sub":"1","email":"anh.tran@example.com","exp":1790329117,"iss":"donhang-api","aud":"donhang-app"} rc=0 (GNU base64 8.32). RFC 7515 sec. 3.1 compact form: "BASE64URL(UTF8(JWS Protected Header)) || '.' || BASE64URL(JWS Payload) || '.' || BASE64URL(JWS Signature)"; sec. 5.1 computes the signature over the JWS Signing Input, then encodes it as BASE64URL(JWS Signature). Supports sec. 3's "raw bytes ... then Base64url-encoded like the others". Lesson now restricts "three parts" to signed JWTs.

RFC 7515 sec. 2: Base64url Encoding = "Base64 encoding using the URL- and filename-safe character set defined in Section 5 of RFC 4648, with all trailing '=' characters omitted" — no key involved. Live: header and payload decoded with base64 -d, no key.

RFC 7518 sec. 3.1 table: "HS256 | HMAC using SHA-256". Sec. 3.2: HMACs combine "a secret plus a cryptographic hash function to generate a MAC", which shows "whoever generated the MAC was in possession of the MAC key".

RFC 7519 sec. 2 NumericDate: "A JSON numeric value representing the number of seconds from 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z UTC until the specified UTC date/time, ignoring leap seconds." Lesson sec. 4 and quiz q5 now name the 1 January 1970 (UTC) reference point.

RFC 7515 sec. 5.2 step 8: validate the decoded signature "against the JWS Signing Input ASCII(BASE64URL(UTF8(JWS Protected Header)) || '.' || BASE64URL(JWS Payload))"; RFC 7518 sec. 3.2: computed HMAC is "compared to the result of base64url decoding the received encoded JWS Signature value". stage-1 Program.cs: AddJwtBearer with IssuerSigningKey. Live: tampered -> 401.
claim_verdicts.source: rfc7515 sec. 5.2; rfc7518 sec. 3.2; stage-1 DonHang.Api/Program.cs; live run

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 7519 sec. 12: "A JWT may contain privacy-sensitive information. When this is the case, measures MUST be taken to prevent disclosure to unintended parties." Lesson sentence is now conditional ("nothing that must stay hidden from whoever gets hold of the token") and follows from claim 5; no longer contradicts the email claim.

RFC 7519 abstract: "a compact, URL-safe means of representing claims"; sec. 1: "intended for space constrained environments such as HTTP Authorization headers and URI query parameters". RFC 4648 sec. 5: values 62/63 are '-' and '_' instead of '+' and '/'; RFC 7515 sec. 2: trailing '=' omitted.
claim_verdicts.source: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7519 abstract, sec. 1; rfc4648 sec. 5; rfc7515 sec. 2

claim_verdicts.evidence: Live (GNU base64 8.32): signature part (43 chars) unpadded -> bytes then `base64: invalid input`; same part + '=' -> 32 bytes, no error. `echo eyJ4IjoiPz8_In0= | tr '_-' '/+' | base64 -d` -> {"x":"???"} rc=0; `echo -_8= | tr '_-' '/+' | base64 -d` -> fb ff. RFC 4648 sec. 5: base64url differs only in chars 62 ('-') and 63 ('_').

Live: `cut -d. -f3 | tr '_-' '/+' | base64 -d | od -c` printed 32 non-text bytes (\247 7 \323 A ...) and `base64: invalid input` (missing '='). Not JSON.

RFC 7518 sec. 3.2: HMAC shows "whoever generated the MAC was in possession of the MAC key" and requires "A key of the same size as the hash output (for instance, 256 bits for 'HS256') or larger". Deterministic and fixed-size confirmed live (signature decodes to 32 bytes). "Nobody can produce it" is absolute; security is computational and depends on key strength (hence the RFC's key-size MUST).
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: "...the same text and key always give the same result, and without the key it is not practically possible to produce it."

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 7518 sec. 3.2: the MAC is generated "using the shared key" and validation recomputes it. SymmetricSecurityKey(byte[] key): parameter "The byte array of the key." stage-1 Program.cs validates with `new SymmetricSecurityKey(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(signingKey))` from the same Jwt:SigningKey that JwtTokenService signs with.

issues.text: Unlisted claims about library behaviour: that SecurityAlgorithms.HmacSha256 becomes "alg":"HS256", and that WriteToken does the encoding and signing. Both are true (WriteToken remarks: "If either SigningCredentials or InnerToken.SigningCredentials are set, the JWT will be signed"; live header {"alg":"HS256",...}), but neither is in the ledger; claim 1 only says the method returns WriteToken(token). Quiz q6 explanation repeats the HmacSha256 -> HS256 mapping.
issues.quote: `SecurityAlgorithms.HmacSha256` is what becomes `"alg":"HS256"` in the header. ... `WriteToken` does the encoding and signing
issues.fix: Add two claims to .meta.json (section 5): (a) "SecurityAlgorithms.HmacSha256 is written as alg HS256 in the header" — source_hint: live decoded header, stage-1; (b) "JwtSecurityTokenHandler.WriteToken serializes the token to compact form and signs it when SigningCredentials are set" — source_hint: learn.microsoft.com JwtSecurityTokenHandler.WriteToken remarks. No text change needed.

issues.text: Absolute wording for HMAC security (claim 16). RFC 7518 ties it to possession of the key and mandates a key of at least 256 bits; producing a MAC without the key is infeasible, not impossible.
issues.quote: and without the key nobody can produce it
issues.fix: Replace with "and without the key it is not practically possible to produce it"; update claim 16 text to "cannot practically be computed without the key".

issues.text: q2 option c (the key) gives an overstated reason. Not every terminal has a Base64 decoder (Windows cmd/PowerShell have no `base64` command), and the lesson itself needs `tr` first because Base64url is not plain Base64. Key is still the only correct option, so not ambiguous.
issues.quote: takes only a decoder that any terminal already has
issues.fix: Change en to "False, because turning the payload back into JSON takes only a decoder and no key at all." and vi to "Sai, vì biến payload trở lại thành JSON chỉ cần một bộ giải mã, không cần key nào."

issues.text: Unlisted characterisation of HMAC-SHA256 as a "one-way computation" in Connections. The body never calls it one-way and no claim covers it; HMAC is a keyed MAC, and the point the lesson makes is key possession, not one-wayness.
issues.quote: another one-way computation used for proof rather than for hiding
issues.fix: Change to "and another computation used for proof rather than for hiding", or add a claim with RFC 2104 as source.

issues.text: Outline item 2 says the login endpoint issues the token after verifying the password hash; the lesson body never states this — it appears only in Connections ("the check that runs right before IssueToken"). Quiz q3 relies on it for step c. True at stage-1: AuthController.Login returns Unauthorized() unless PasswordHasher.Verify succeeds, then calls IssueToken.
issues.quote: the same string `AuthController.Login` returns as the `token` field, and nothing about it is saved
issues.fix: Extend to: "— the same string `AuthController.Login` returns as the `token` field, and only after `PasswordHasher.Verify` has accepted the password; nothing about it is saved." Add to claim 14: "Login calls IssueToken only after PasswordHasher.Verify succeeds" (source AuthController.cs:16-22).

issues.text: HMAC, SHA-256, HMAC-SHA256 and HS256 are never explained. The lesson only expands HS256 into two more unknown names. I can follow 'computed with the signing key', but the name appears in the diagram, sec. 5, summary line 3 and quiz q3/q6, and I cannot tell whether it is a library, a rule, or the calculation itself.
issues.quote: The header says how the token is signed — here `"alg":"HS256"`, HMAC with SHA-256.
issues.fix: Add one sentence after this one: 'HMAC-SHA256 is just the name of the calculation the API uses to make the signature: it takes text plus a key and always gives the same short result for the same inputs, and without the key you cannot produce that result.'

issues.text: 'Encrypted' is not in what I know (I know encoding). The first misconception, summary line 2 ('encoded, not encrypted') and quiz q2/q4 all hinge on the contrast, but the lesson never says what encrypted means, so I learn only 'encoding is not the other thing'.
issues.quote: A JWT's payload is encrypted, so its claims can't be read without the API's signing key.
issues.fix: Where 'encrypted' first appears, add a short clause in plain words: 'encrypted — scrambled so that only someone holding a key can turn it back into readable text'. Or replace 'encrypted' everywhere with that phrase.
